tips.hello: Hello, I am Ms Turtle the teacher. This game is called Tapko, and it teaches you to type with all ten fingers. Now and then I will tell you here what Tapko can do.
tips.help: When you are not sure what to do, click the question mark at the top right or press F1. Help shows what each button does.
tips.keyboard: You can use all of Tapko without a mouse: Tab and the arrows move between buttons, Enter confirms, Esc closes a window, and in a level F2 hides the keyboard on the screen.
tips.progress: Click Tapko or My progress. You will see which keys you know, your badges and how you are getting better.
tips.task: You have a task from your teacher! You will find it on the map. When you finish it, Tapko gives you a link with the result: send it back to your teacher.
tips.share: You can show your results to your teacher or parents: in My progress you send them as a link or a QR code.
tips.range: Every world you finish opens the Target range and the Parrot on the map. At the range you practise the letters that are not easy yet.

intro: Hello {name}! This is your character in this adventure.
You will learn to type with all ten fingers.
world1: It is a lovely afternoon on the meadow. There is a football match later!
The animals train with you: they kick leaves like a ball and you keep goal.
Catch the leaves with letters: type the word on a leaf and the leaf is yours.
invitation: The afternoon on the meadow is over. Look what you found in the grass!
Your fingers are ready for a rocket flight.
world2: You fly off to explore a few planets, all the way to the dragons' planet.
Your typing rhythm drives the rocket and a soft beam pushes meteors out of the way.
landing: The dragons' planet is in sight. The control tower says: landing clearance granted!
We are landing... oh no, right in a swamp!
world3: Welcome to the dragons' planet! Its crystal of life has lost its light.
Cross the swamp and the meadow, find the crystals of life and wake them with a spell.
Then carry them to the Cradle of Life. Careful typing matters more than speed here.
force: The crystals of life shine and the whole planet blooms again!
To thank you, they gave you the Force: you move things gently, just by typing.
The dragons in the next valley need help.
world4: Space rocks are falling into the Dragon Valley.
Every word makes a shield bubble for a baby dragon.
The rocks just bounce away, nobody gets hurt.
egg: The dragons are safe and happy.
As a thank you, they give you a magical Dragon Egg!
world5: Oh! The egg starts to wiggle and roll down the hill.
Help it jump over rocks and stumps.
Watch out for a friendly mole!
hatched: A tiny baby dragon looks at you. You have a new friend!
Now you can go on rescue missions and help more dragons.
world6: You walk past an old junkyard. What is that beeping?
Someone is beeping sadly under a pile of old things.
Type a word and a soft magnet lifts the junk off the pile.
friends: A small rusty robot climbs out of the pile.
He wants to say thank you, but he can only beep: Beep beep!
He gives you a tiny gear. His name is Bolt, and now you are friends!
world7: Bolt wants to go home, but he is missing some parts.
Gears, bolts and springs ride along the conveyor belt.
Type a part's word and toss it into the basket.
legs: Done! Bolt has new long legs.
And a bright new yellow antenna on his head.
Now he can walk the long way home.
world8: Oh no, it starts to rain!
Robots must not get wet, or they rust.
Type the word on a raindrop and your umbrella catches it.
raincoat: The rain stopped and a rainbow shines over the town.
Bolt gets a yellow raincoat and you a new umbrella.
Now no rain can hurt you two.
world9: The way home leads through Robot City.
All doors are locked and the panels show passwords.
Type a password and the door opens with a chime.
key: Bolt found the key card to his home.
world10: Bolt's home is dark and all the robots are asleep.
Type a word and a lamp switches on.
The helper robots wake up and wave hello.
home: Bolt's family is so happy he is home.
They thank you, {name}, for helping Bolt.
Now you can repair little robots on rescue missions too.
world11: The forest has gone quiet. Not a bird sings, not a leaf rustles.
A tiny fairy with shimmering wings flies up to you. "I am Melody. The forest forgot its songs!"
Type a word and a sleeping bud opens. Each flower hums one note.
wreath: The big flower is awake and the whole garden hums!
Melody weaves you a flower wreath.
The garden has its song back. One song is home, four more to go.
world12: The birds on the forest path forgot their words.
Each bird sings a word quietly. Listen well and type what you hear.
Tap a bird's word if you want to hear it again.
feather: Who, who? The owl liked your answers.
She gives you a soft feather for your hat.
world13: The lake is still as a mirror.
A word shows on the water, then a little wave washes it away.
Remember it and type it, and a lily blooms.
lily: The long reflection is back in the water!
Melody gives you a shining water lily.
The frogs croak the lake's song.
world14: In the middle of the forest stands the Music Tree.
Its notes hang on the branches. Some sing, some glow and then fade.
Listen or remember, then type, and the note flies up.
harp: The Music Tree plays its song again!
Melody gives you a little harp.
Only one song is missing, the song of the night.
world15: The moon rises and the fireflies come to the ball.
Melody sings a short sentence for each firefly.
Type it and the dance floor lights up.
wings: The whole forest sings! Every bird, every frog, every tree.
The forest thanks you, {name}. Melody gives you fairy wings.
Now you can also guide little birds and fireflies home on rescue missions.

junkStart: Can you hear that beeping? Someone is under the pile!

knotOpen: The knot is untied! Bolt is free.
Beep beep! That means thank you.
batteryFull: The battery is full! Bolt is glowing with joy.

stormCalm: The storm calmed down. Here comes the sun!

owlSolved: The owl is happy, the birds are singing!

about.report: Report a bug or an idea
about.intro: TapkoTyper (Tapko) is a free, peaceful game that teaches typing with all ten fingers. As an animal of their own choice, keyboard typing students travel through worlds full of adventures. Nothing bad ever happens: obstacles are pushed away or helped, never destroyed.
privacy: No ads, purchases, sign-in or cookies. This site has no server of its own in the background.
All progress is stored **only in this browser** and nobody else can reach it, but you can export it to a file to back it up or move it to another computer.

After the first visit, or as a desktop app, it works without the internet too. {install} as a desktop web app, it opens in its own window without the whole browser, works offline and is quick and easy to start.
about.dataTitle: Your data and the visit counter
data: Because everything is only on your computer, we cannot recover a forgotten settings password, or your settings and progress when your computer breaks. So export your progress to a file now and then. If you forget the password anyway, read the {readme} file on GitHub.

We only count anonymous visits, without cookies and without any data about users (of course nothing is counted if you use it offline). The counting is done by GoatCounter, which uses no cookies and collects no personal data. The downside is that we cannot tell which parts of the app are used and which are not.
about.visitsOne: So far we have recorded {n} visit.
about.visitsFew: So far we have recorded {n} visits.
about.visitsMany: So far we have recorded {n} visits.
how: Keys are learned one by one, starting from the home row (F and J).
Every key has its finger; the on-screen keyboard and hands show which one.
Accuracy comes first; speed is only shown as a personal trend.
Weak keys appear more often, and short breaks keep sessions healthy.
It is played on a real keyboard; a phone or tablet needs a keyboard connected. A typing teacher or a parent with a phone and no keyboard can still scan the results.

help.title: Help
type: TapkoTyper needs a real keyboard. Connect one to a phone or tablet over Bluetooth or USB.
Sit up straight, feet on the floor, shoulders relaxed.
Feel the **little bumps on F and J**. Your index fingers live there.
The other fingers lie next to them on the middle row: A S D F and J K L {pinky}.
Your thumbs rest above the space bar.
Each finger has its own keys. After every letter it goes back home.
Look at **the screen, not at your hands**. The keyboard below shows which finger goes.
**First type correctly**, then fast. Speed comes by itself.
After a little while of play, take a break: stand up, stretch and drink some water.

icons.fullscreen: Play on the whole screen and back again.
icons.update: The red button at the far right shows up when a new version of the game is ready. Click it to install it.
icons.timer: The clock in the wardrobe shows how much time you have left. While there is plenty, it smiles; then a number drops by one every 10 seconds. When it blinks, the time is nearly over. When the time is up, it shows a lock, and its tip says how much more practice you need. You earn wardrobe time by practising.
icons.pause: Pause. The **Esc key** pauses too. In the pause you can end the level; once something is typed it asks first, because the level will not count.
icons.paw: The paw shows whether your help is ready: every word without a mistake fills a bit of the ring, after {n} words the paw is charged. Press **Enter** when you are stuck and your paw types {words} words for you.
icons.ring: The ring with the number shows which level of the world this is. Green pieces fill up to this level, empty ones are still to come. At the last one, the big challenge, it is full.
icons.progress: The bar shows how much of the level is behind you.
icons.gauge: The green ring shows your rhythm. When you type smoothly, it fills up.
icons.levelHelp: Help: what to do in this level and how to type. **F1** opens it too.
icons.super: The star at the top: super mode. It opens the service menu.
icons.read: Read aloud: the computer reads the words to you. **F3** turns it on or off.
icons.guide: Shows or hides the keyboard that tells where the finger goes. **F2** does it too.
icons.menu: On a small screen these buttons hide under one Menu button.
icons.theme: Dark or light mode for the whole game. The moon turns it on, the sun brings the light back. Until someone switches it, it follows the device.
icons.language: The game's language, on the start page. Opens the list of languages.

card: Click yourself, your character, and My progress opens: what you already do well and what to practise.
Warm-up: a short stretch (you can add the big warm-up), then the next level starts.
Continue starts the next level of the story.
Own typing: a short exercise on the keys you pick.
My text: when a parent adds their own text, you type all of it in order.
Just typing: type anything, you walk through a world you choose and see what you typed.
Me and my wardrobe: pick your character and nickname and dress up in the things you unlocked.
Rescue missions and Little friends: they appear after you finish your first story.
Today's task: when your teacher sends a task, you find it on the card. When it is done, you hand it in.
progress: Key, world and story: how many keys you type well and fast (at least 9 of 10 presses right), how many worlds and stories you have finished.

The target is your accuracy over the last 14 days, the arrow of keys your speed in characters per minute, the star all the stars you have earned, and the pile of keys the letters you typed in the last 14 days.
Each story row shows its worlds: finished ones in colour, the rest grey, and the stars of that story.
Parrot: how many parrots are at home now and the most there were at once. Flown ones come back when you play with them again.
Open My progress with its button on the map. It has four tabs: Progress, Keys, Levels and Exercises. A click on your character shows a quick look.
Keys shows which keys go well and which to practise. You can start practice right from there.
A **QR code** shows your progress or an exercise to your teacher: they just take a photo of it. You can print a **Certificate** with your results.
help.moreTitle: Rescue mission, target range, parrot and badge
more: Rescue mission: a short task where you help a little friend. It opens when you finish the first story, and you find it on the map.
Badge: you get one for every finished world. The more stars you collect in that world, the nicer it is: bronze, silver, gold.

Target range: when you finish a world, a target appears on the map next to its big challenge. Tapko throws funny things at the target and you type the words on the rings they fly through. You practise the letters you do not type accurately enough yet.
Type every word in time and without a mistake and you hit the middle. A mistake makes the thing fly a little lower, and after three it falls to the ground. Nothing bad happens, the next one comes.

Every world has a rare thing of its own at the range. Hit it in the middle and throw to the end, and it joins your collection. Then **Enter** puts it in Tapko's paw instead of the thing that is there.

Parrot: when you finish a world, a parrot joins its target. You type a few words many times in a row and the parrot repeats them after you, until your fingers know them by themselves. Speed does not matter.
Parrots fly away after a while, so come back and play again. When the parrots of all your finished worlds are at home, you have the **Parrot badge** next to your name.
play: Type the word on the object. Then it clears the way.
When a word gets away, nothing bad happens. Another one comes.
Started typing a word you did not want? **Backspace** wipes it and you can start any word again.
Stars come from **accuracy**: the fewer mistakes, the more stars.
When you type well, new letters come.
**Esc** stops the game and another Esc lets it go on.

games.intro: The small picture on a level's circle on the map shows which game waits there.
games.chase: **Word stream**: words fly or roll toward you. Type them before they arrive.
games.catch: **Waiting words**: words wait calmly, for example above poppy buds. Each starts with a different letter, so pick the one you type.
games.crossroads: **Crossroads**: at a crossroads the word you type picks the way.
games.clean: **Copy**: words stand in a row and you type them from left to right. On the invitation a mistake makes the word fade and two new ones come: more practice, not a punishment.
games.listen: **Dictation**: you do not see the word, you only hear it. Type what you hear. When you wait a while, it is said again.
games.remember: **Secret words**: a word shows only for a moment and hides. Remember it and type it from memory.
games.aim: **Target range**: words full of the letters you still miss. Each word throws a thing through the rings into the target.
games.parrot: **Parrot**: a few words many times in a row. The parrot repeats each one. A slip brings the word twice more.
games.super: **Big challenge**: the last level of a world. Every world has its own.

journey: The game has stories. Each story has worlds, and each world has a few levels.
You play the levels in order. At the end of a world a big challenge waits.
Every level gives you up to **three stars**. The fewer mistakes, the more stars.
You can play a level again when you want more stars.
New letters come when the old ones go well. Some levels and stories open only when you know enough letters.
When you miss a letter, practise it in Own typing.
task: Your teacher can send you a task as a link. Open it and choose who does it.
On the map you see Today's task. Type until the time is up.
When it is done, press Hand in and send your teacher the **result link**.
help.settingsIntro: The settings are for the teacher or parent. They open with the gear. Until you **lock them with a password**, anyone opens them by clicking a simple confirm button.

settings: Student: nickname, character and optional name, game language, word language and keyboard layout. Pick the layout of the real keyboard; the finger guide follows it.
Practice: difficulty and word length. In automatic mode they grow with the student; set them by hand when you want.
Words without diacritics help beginners for a while. No time pressure makes moving things stop and wait for the student.
Session length before a break: then the game invites the student to a short rest.
Finger guide: fades when keys are mastered, or always on or off. You can lock it for the student.
Wardrobe time earned by practice: 1 minute in the wardrobe for 5 minutes of practice, at most 7 minutes. Turned off, the wardrobe is always open.

Sounds and interface: volumes, font, large text, reduced motion, high contrast, fullscreen. **Translate the game** opens the translator page: translate the game into a new language there, or change its texts to your own.
The settings password locks the settings for every player on this device. We cannot recover a forgotten password.

The password protects the settings only inside the game. All data (players, progress and settings) is stored in this browser and the password does not encrypt it. Anyone who gets to it directly, for example with the browser's developer tools, can read and change it.
Anyone who uses this computer can clear the site's data in the browser. That removes every player, their progress, the results and the password. So export your progress to a file now and then.
own: Own words: for example this week's spelling words. They are used even with keys the student does not know yet.
Own text: split into sentences and parts. On the map, the My text button types all of it in order.
Own encouragements: the game says them now and then.
How much of own words and text: the share of targets in levels.
surprises: Hide a real reward behind a rule: after a level, after minutes of training, after more levels or stars, or at random.
The game asks the question before a level and tells the answer once the rule is met.
task: For typing teachers and parents: make a task with words or a text and a length. You get a link and a QR code.
Students open the link and, when done, send you a result link. You see the results with the For teachers button on the start page.
keys: Automatic: keys come one by one, starting from the home row F and J. This is best.
By hand: pick the keys the student learns, punctuation too.
data: Everything is stored **only in this browser**. When the browser's data is cleared or the computer breaks, the progress is lost unless you have a backup.
So **export the profile** to a file now and then. Import loads it back, or on another device.
Move to another computer: the whole profile is inside a link. A guest profile is forgotten when the tab closes.

keys: The app can be used without a mouse too. **Enter** or the **space bar** presses the lit button, **Tab** and the **arrows** move between buttons.
Pick your player by its number **1 to 9**.
**F1** opens help, **F2** shows or hides the keyboard, **F3** turns reading aloud on or off.
**F4** switches the sound: normal, quiet, off. **F8** plays another song.
**Esc** closes the window on top. Otherwise it pauses or resumes a level, and goes back from other screens.
mentor: Open the **For teachers** page with the chart icon at the top right of the start page. Results are stored only in this browser.
Scanning is fastest: type a group (for example 5A), press **Scan QR** and walk around the room. The camera reads several QR codes at once and puts every new result into this group.
A student shows the QR code in My progress or after handing in a task. Without a camera, paste or open the **result link**.

A **set** is the results of one group that came together: one camera scan, or links added within **20 minutes** of the first. The **Groups** tab shows each group's sets; click a day to see the set's students, and download it all as CSV.

Every hand-in is kept. On the **Students** tab, find a student by name and see how accuracy and rhythm changed from the first hand-in to the last. Click a name to see the progress in charts and every hand-in.

**From a phone to a computer:** on the **Files** tab, press **Send to a computer** on the phone and send yourself the .tapko file (by e-mail, for example). On the computer, load it on the same tab or drop it on the page. What you already have is not added twice.
Results older than a **year** are deleted when the page opens. Old results loaded from a file stay for **7 days** more. Delete sooner with **Delete…**.
The checksum shows a damaged link (an exclamation mark by the name), not cheating.
Create a task for students in the settings, on the Task tab: you get a link and a QR code for the students to open.

tips.sit-straight: Sit up straight and lean your back on the chair.
tips.feet-floor: Keep your feet flat on the floor or on a footrest.
tips.elbows-close: Keep your elbows near your body, not flying out.
tips.right-angles: Bend your elbows and knees at about a right angle.
tips.sit-higher: Sitting too low? Put a cushion under you.
tips.screen-distance: Keep the screen about an arm's length away.
tips.screen-height: Put the screen at eye level so your neck stays relaxed.
tips.relax-shoulders: Drop your shoulders, breathe out and relax your hands.
tips.wrists-float: Let your wrists float lightly, not bent.
tips.no-palms: Don't lean on your palms, keep your hands light.
tips.soft-touch: Press keys softly, no need to bang.
tips.thumbs-rest: Let your thumbs hover over the space bar.
tips.fj-bumps: Feel the bumps on F and J, your index fingers rest there.
tips.home-row: Home is the middle row: A S D F and J K L {pinky}.
tips.return-home: After every letter, send your finger back home.
tips.one-finger: Every letter has its own finger, always the same one.
tips.index-two: Your index fingers do the most, two columns each.
tips.middle-ei: Your middle finger reaches E and I, then goes right back.
tips.pinky-p: Your right pinky reaches P, then goes back to the home row.
tips.ring-finger: Your ring finger is clever: S, L, W and the dot are its.
tips.reach-t: For the far T, stretch your index finger and return to F.
tips.feel-center: Aim for the middle of the key, even without looking.
tips.thumb-space: Press Space with the thumb that did not just type.
tips.shift-opposite: For a capital letter, press Shift with the pinky of the other hand.
tips.capital-a: You type A with the left hand, so press the right Shift.
tips.yz-swap: On a Slovak keyboard, Z is on top and Y is below.
tips.z-finger: Your right index types Z and your left pinky types Y.
tips.number-row: The number row holds ľ š č ť ž ý á í é, add Shift for digits.
tips.number-fingers: Type the top row with the same finger as the letters below it.
tips.dead-keys: Press the accent mark first, then the letter.
tips.caron-shift: The caron is typed with the same key as the acute accent, but with Shift.
tips.accent-pinky: The keys ú ä ô ň belong to your right pinky.
tips.diacritics-fun: Slovak accents are a little magic. You are learning it!
tips.eyes-screen: Look at the screen, your fingers will find the way.
tips.no-peeking: Tempted to peek at the keyboard? Picture the finger instead.
tips.rest-eyes: Look out the window sometimes, your eyes need rest too.
tips.accuracy-first: Be accurate first, speed will come by itself.
tips.steady-beat: Type in a steady beat, like tapping along to a song.
tips.slow-down: Making many mistakes? Slow down and it gets easier.
tips.hard-word: Type a tricky word a few times in a row, slowly at first.
tips.mistakes-ok: Mistakes are fine, you learn something from each one.
tips.patience: Feel like you're not improving? That's normal, keep going.
tips.short-sessions: A few short practices beat one long one.
tips.stretch-fingers: On a short break, spread your fingers, make fists, then open them again.
tips.stretch-wrist: On a short break, bend your wrist and gently press it with the other hand.
tips.take-break: After a few minutes, stand up, stretch and drink some water.
tips.celebrate: When it goes well, you can be proud of yourself.
tips.listen-whole: Listen to the whole word first, then type it.
tips.listen-again: Did not catch it? Tap the word and you will hear it again.
tips.listen-sounds: Say the word quietly to yourself, letter by letter.
tips.remember-picture: Look at the whole word like a picture before it hides.
tips.remember-wait: Wait until the word hides, then type it from memory.
tips.remember-slip: Forgot a letter? A mistake shows the word for a moment again.
